rationale: This cross-national panel study (31 Sub-Saharan African countries, 1990-2005, N=70 country-year observations) uses two-way fixed effects OLS and instrumental-variable regressions to test the effect of aggregate per-capita IMF structural adjustment loan amounts on infant mortality rates. Although the narrative background mentions subsidy cuts, health/education user fees, and asset privatization among broad macroeconomic structural adjustment conditionalities, no water or sanitation legal/regulatory rule-type mechanism is empirically operationalized or tested (NONE_NO_RULE_MECHANISM). Likewise, the sole dependent variable across all models in Tables 1 and 2 is infant mortality (a health outcome), while national access to an improved water and sanitation source enters only as a right-hand-side independent/mediating covariate rather than an analyzed access outcome (NONE_NO_ACCESS_OUTCOME). The longitudinal country-panel regression design using secondary macro indicators is observational.
